history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 602 / 'Shri Mahalaxmi Devi Temple' (id: shri-mahalakshmi-devi-temple-nagpur) - the same Koradi Mahalakshmi Jagdamba Mandir already researched in an earlier Nagpur batch. The CSV row 'Koradi Temple, Nagpur' resolves to the Shri Mahalakshmi Jagdamba Mandir at Koradi, the most celebrated Mahalaxmi shrine of the Nagpur region. Legend says the place was once Jakhapur, ruled by King Jholan, whose daughter Jakhumai was recognised as Adi Shakti; after leading his army to victory she halted to rest at Jakhapur at sunset and vanished, leaving a self-manifested idol of Mahalakshmi Jagdamba where she rested. The goddess is worshipped in three forms through the day (young girl in the morning, youthful woman in the afternoon, elderly woman at night), and devotees report the setting sun's rays falling on the idol on certain days in March and September (verify). She is the Kuldevi (family deity) of the Vidarbha community, and the temple is regarded by devotees as one of the 51 Shakti-peeths (a devotional claim, not epigraphically established). The complex has been extensively renovated in recent decades and now includes a Ramayana museum/centre and lies on the banks of Koradi Lake.

name: Koradi Temple

town_description: Koradi is a small temple town in Nagpur district, about 13-15 km north of Nagpur city centre, best known for the Mahalakshmi Jagdamba temple and Koradi Lake beside it. It is also the site of the Koradi Thermal Power Station, one of the region's major power plants. Despite the industrial backdrop, the temple precinct draws lakhs of pilgrims, especially during Navratri.
